claims.text: PVP moderately slows the reduction kinetics of the Pt, Pd, Au, Ag, and Cu precursors.
Slowing reduction with PVP synchronizes nucleation and growth across the five metals.
Synchronized nucleation and growth yield nanoparticles with uniform atomic-scale distributions of all five elements.
Atomic-scale compositional homogeneity enhances CO oxidation activity.
The catalytic enhancement from compositional homogeneity arises from optimized adsorption-desorption energetics.
PVP binds transiently to all five metal species.
Transient PVP binding reduces the individual reduction rates of all five metal species.
PVP narrows the differences among the reduction-onset potentials of the five metal species.
Coincident nucleation of the metals prevents early phase-segregated growth.
Homogeneous STEM-EDS elemental maps establish atomic-scale uniform mixing within each nanoparticle.
PVP-treated synthesis will produce a particle-size distribution of 5 ± 1 nm.
PVP-treated nanoparticles will have approximately twice the CO oxidation turnover frequency of uncapped nanoparticles.
Nanoparticles synthesized without PVP have a bimodal size distribution.
Nanoparticles synthesized without PVP contain phase-segregated domains, such as Au-rich cores and Cu-rich shells.
Nanoparticles synthesized without PVP have lower CO oxidation turnover frequency than PVP-treated nanoparticles.
The hypothesis is expected to hold when precursor standard reduction potentials differ by no more than 0.3 V.
The hypothesis is expected to hold for PVP concentrations from 0.01 M to 0.1 M.
The hypothesis is expected to hold at synthesis temperatures from 130 to 150 °C.
The hypothesis is expected to hold for hydrothermal reaction times from 2 to 6 hours.
